claim: The default security standards that Security Hub CSPM can enable automatically are the AWS Foundational Security Best Practices standard and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v1.2.0 standard; with local configuration they are enabled for new member accounts when they join, and you can turn this off.
question: Which Security Hub CSPM standards are enabled by default?

values.display: the AWS Foundational Security Best Practices standard

values.spoken: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark version one point two

qualifiers.condition: local configuration with AWS Organizations; central configuration uses a policy instead

evidence.quote: Currently, the default security standards are the AWS Foundational Security Best Practices standard and the Center for Internet Security (CIS) AWS Foundations Benchmark v1.2.0 standard.
With local configuration, AWS Security Hub CSPM can automatically enable default security standards for new member accounts when the accounts join your organization.

claim: When you enable the new Security Hub, it automatically enables Security Hub CSPM in your account; Inspector and GuardDuty capabilities are enabled as a next step, and Amazon Macie is not automatically enabled.
question: What does enabling the new Security Hub turn on automatically?

values.display: it automatically enables Security Hub CSPM in your account
Amazon Macie for sensitive data discovery is not automatically enabled.

evidence.quote: When you enable Security Hub, it automatically enables Security Hub CSPM in your account for posture management.
Amazon Macie for sensitive data discovery is not automatically enabled.
